description: Presentations on Social Engineering at DEF CON 23 explores human-layer vulnerabilities, open-source intelligence gathering, digital surveillance tradecraft, lock pattern predictability, and identity fraud.

talks.title: Michael Schrenk - Applied Intelligence: Using Information Thats Not There
talks.teaser: Michael Schrenk demonstrates negative space analysis in OSINT, identifying organizational secrets and covert operations from missing data.

talks.title: Marte Loge - Tell me who you are and I will tell you your lock pattern
talks.teaser: Marte Løge analyzes Android lock patterns, demonstrating how demographic and psychological traits make user unlock gestures predictable.

talks.title: Ken Westin - Confessions of a Professional Cyber Stalker
talks.teaser: Ken Westin shares ethical dilemmas, investigative tradecraft, and tracking techniques developed while hunting stolen devices and cyber criminals.

talks.title: Chris Rock
talks.teaser: Chris Rock examines systemic vulnerabilities in death registration, hospital records, and probate courts used to legally declare individuals deceased.
